Walton's opening letters are addressed 'To Mrs. Saville, England' (his sister Margaret Saville) — Victor is never the addressee; he is a rescued stranger whose spoken narrative Walton records within those same letters. This is exactly the risk flagged in the task brief. Minimal fix: 'письма Роберта Уолтона адресованы его сестре Маргарет Сэвилл, а внутри этих писем сам Виктор рассказывает Уолтону, как попытался произвести жизнь.' No other change needed in that paragraph.

CONFIRMED ACCURATE on independent primary-source check: creature unnamed in 1818 text (Gutenberg + Oxford page); anonymous 1818 edition and Prometheus subtitle (Oxford page); AFI Catalog 1931 film credits Colin Clive as 'Henry Frankenstein' and Karloff as 'The Monster', correctly distinguished from the novel (checked directly on AFI catalog page). Saxophone: single-reed mechanism, brass-but-woodwind classification, Adolphe Sax/1840s, clarinet fingering/embouchure similarity — all match Yamaha 'Woodwind Family Explained' and 'Structure of the Saxophone' pages verbatim. Flute: lip/embouchure edge-tone mechanism, contrast with reed instruments and with recorder end-blown design — match Yamaha 'Structure of the Flute' and 'Woodwind Family Explained'; minor note: draft's phrase 'ветряной канал' (duct) for the recorder is a reasonable gloss, not a literal quote from the cited Yamaha wording ('blown from the end') — not an error, just imprecise sourcing.

No answer-option hints/duplicate alternatives, no long copyrighted quotes, source variety and primary-source emphasis all look correct on inspection. report:
Review complete and reported to Root.

**Verdict: REWORK** (1 confirmed factual error out of 3 articles)

- **Article 003 (Frankenstein)** — error found: the draft claims "Robert Walton addresses his letter to 'Victor Frankenstein'." Checked against Project Gutenberg's 1818 text — Walton's opening letters are addressed "To Mrs. Saville, England" (his sister Margaret), not to Victor. Victor is a rescued stranger whose spoken narrative Walton records within those same letters. Proposed a minimal one-sentence fix in the task review note. All other claims in that article (unnamed creature, anonymous 1818 edition, Prometheus theme, 1931 AFI film crediting "Henry Frankenstein"/"The Monster") checked out against Oxford and AFI Catalog pages.
- **Articles 007 (saxophone) and 017 (flute)** — all substantive claims (single-reed mechanism, brass-but-woodwind classification, Adolphe Sax/1840s, clarinet comparison, flute embouchure/edge-tone mechanism, recorder contrast) verified against Yamaha's instrument-guide pages and are accurate.
- Revision SHA256 for all three articles matched the published snapshot exactly; status fields correct; no answer-option hints, duplicate alternatives, or long quotes found.

Review note and verdict submitted via `hub_task review`; summary sent to Root (session-27aed86cfdf24a7ca4f3872e17b6d4b4). Stopping here per scope (finite 3-article review, no edits made).
